content.intro: This lesson covers understanding data in ai through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Build the mental model behind AI, machine learning, deep learning, data, training, inference, and evaluation. Keep predictive and generative tasks distinct.

items.title: Text, images, audio, video, and sensor data
items.text: Text, images, audio, video, and sensor data concerns a modality-specific input or output path. Check supported formats, dimensions/duration, preprocessing, provenance, and any relevant consent or licensing constraints; assess output quality with criteria suited to that modality instead of relying on a single text-based score.

items.title: Datasets, examples, and data distributions
items.text: For datasets, examples, and data distributions, distinguish the training objective from the evaluation goal. Check provenance and data quality, keep validation/test examples isolated from training, record the baseline and configuration, and evaluate both improvement on the target task and possible regressions elsewhere.

items.title: Data quality and coverage
items.text: Use data quality and coverage to turn a vague quality claim into an observable criterion. Define a representative dataset, an expected outcome or rubric, a baseline, and the failure categories you will record; interpret aggregate scores alongside examples and affected groups.

items.title: Missing, noisy, and duplicated data
items.text: Missing, noisy, and duplicated data addresses how information is prepared, described, versioned, or governed. Validate the input, keep source and access metadata, handle duplicates and missing values deliberately, and test the downstream effect of a data change rather than treating the data pipeline as invisible plumbing.

items.title: Data leakage and its consequences
items.text: Data leakage and its consequences is part of the representation and generation mechanism. Follow the information flow from input representation to model computation to output selection, then distinguish the architecture's capabilities from limits caused by data, context, decoding choices, or compute.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice structured and unstructured data within understanding data in ai: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
